proved_step: Let F be a CNF on n variables whose primal graph has a supplied tree decomposition of width t with O(n) bags. Then F has a deterministic decomposable NNF of size n·2^{O(t)}. Proof: Convert the decomposition to a rooted nice tree decomposition with O(n) bags and width t. At each bag, use one gate for every assignment to its at most t+1 variables that satisfies all clauses assigned at that bag. For each bag assignment, the gate represents precisely the assignments to variables introduced in its subtree that extend the bag assignment and satisfy all clauses assigned in that subtree. At an introduce or forget node, connect gates to the child gates whose assignments agree on the shared variables; when a variable is forgotten, OR the child gates for its two values. These OR inputs represent disjoint assignments because they differ on the forgotten variable. At a join, AND the two child gates agreeing with the parent bag assignment; the children’s variables outside the bag are disjoint, so this AND is decomposable. The root ORs the accepting root-bag assignments; distinct assignments are disjoint. Induction up the decomposition proves that the root represents exactly the satisfying assignments of F. Each bag has at most 2^{t+1} states and each state has at most 2^{O(t)} local connections, so total size is O(n·2^{O(t)}). This is an upper bound for the stated CNF class and decomposition representation; it does not imply a bound for arbitrary perfect-matching graphs.
